record.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063 — When eventType.destinationCalendar is set, the organizer's own destination is skipped while each other host's is appended; if that calendar belongs to another host, that host gets a duplicate event and the organizer gets none.

adjudication.rationale: In handleNewBooking.ts, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized as `[eventType.destinationCalendar]` when eventType.destinationCalendar is set (lines around `destinationCalendar: eventType.destinationCalendar ? [eventType.destinationCalendar] : ...`). Then for COLLECTIVE team event types, it appends `teamDestinationCalendars` gathered from `users.slice(1)` (excluding the organizer) where each user's `user.destinationCalendar` is pushed (around the new `teamDestinationCalendars`/`teamMemberPromises` logic and `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`). If `eventType.destinationCalendar` corresponds to one of those non-organizer hosts, that same destination calendar will be appended again, producing a duplicate entry and thus potentially creating two events for that host in `createAllCalendarEvents` (which iterates over `event.destinationCalendar`). Meanwhile the organizer’s own destination calendar is not added in this branch at all, so the organizer can end up with no event created in their calendar.
